title: Knowing God as Father.  Part 2
scripture_text: “Watch out! Don’t do your good deeds publicly, to be admired by others, for you will lose the reward from your Father in heaven. When you give to someone in need, don’t do as the hypocrites do—blowing trumpets in the synagogues and streets to call attention to their acts of charity! I tell you the truth, they have received all the reward they will ever get. But when you give to someone in need, don’t let your left hand know what your right hand is doing. Give your gifts in private, and your Father, who sees everything, will reward you.
devotional:
“When you pray, don’t be like the hypocrites who love to pray publicly on street corners and in the synagogues where everyone can see them. I tell you the truth, that is all the reward they will ever get. But when you pray, go away by yourself, shut the door behind you, and pray to your Father in private. Then your Father, who sees everything, will reward you. “When you pray, don’t babble on and on as the Gentiles do. They think their prayers are answered merely by repeating their words again and again. Don’t be like them, for your Father knows exactly what you need even before you ask him! Pray like this: Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy. May your Kingdom come soon. May your will be done on earth, as it is in heaven. Give us today the food we need and forgive us our sins, as we have forgiven those who sin against us. And don’t let us yield to temptation, but rescue us from the evil one. “If you forgive those who sin against you, your heavenly Father will forgive you. But if you refuse to forgive others, your Father will not forgive your sins.

“And when you fast, don’t make it obvious, as the hypocrites do, for they try to look miserable and dishevelled so people will admire them for their fasting. I tell you the truth, that is the only reward they will ever get. But when you fast, comb your hair and wash your face. Then no one will notice that you are fasting, except your Father, who knows what you do in private. And your Father, who sees everything, will reward you.

What can we learn about God being our Father from this chapter?

The spiritual disciplines we practice must be done in the context of enjoying God as father. It is so easy to reduce our relationship with God into a religious box-ticking exercise where reputation becomes more important than intimacy. These people became religious, doing the right things in the wrong way, and gradually they became trapped in a need to get their affirmation and approval from others because they had not grasped the fact that God is their father. When people loose their way spiritually, it is not because they are bad people, but their waywardness may be traced back to the fact that they have ceased to believe that God is a loving father.

As God is our Father, then we need to be real and honest before him. When we are told that we should do our acts of righteousness in secret, it would be very easy to put a literal translation on this and think you should only pray in a private place, but that misses the point.

Someone could do something in secret and still have a heart of a hypocrite. The secret refers to an attitude that is the opposite to that of the hypocrite. Sometimes we act before God in the same way the hypocrites come before men. They acted in a certain way to get the approval and praise of men. They acted out of unreality in order to impress others; they were not being real or honest.

Sometimes that is how we come before God, we think we need to impress him, we need to win his approval, we are not honest about ourselves, and we have the same heart attitudes as the hypocrite who engages in a public performance. Our father is looking for authenticity not performance.

I should also mention that we all have an inspired need from time to time to shut the door to the world and everything else and be alone with God because we love him and long to give ourselves to him.

As our Father, God wants to enrich our lives.

There is a very interesting play on words that we don’t pick up in our English translations. ‘’I tell you the truth, they have received all the reward they will ever get.’’

The word that is used for the reward that the hypocrite receives from other people, and the word for reward that is used to describe the father’s response to authentic spirituality are different. The reward of the hypocrite is misthos which was used to describe a persons wage or salary, it is the same word used to describe a hired hand. Misthos describes the heart of the taker. These people thought in terms of deserving something, they had a ‘You owe me’ mindset. They treat God like an employer who owes them something for their good behaviour.

The other word apodidomi reflects the heart of the giver. ‘’Then your Father, who sees everything, will reward you.’’ When the father rewards his children it is his deep expression of his pleasure and delight. The father finds great joy and satisfaction. The rewards that the father gives his children are to teach us about his heart. They are a deep expression of God’s satisfaction and pleasure. The reward is the Joy of God’s heart flowing over into ours.

Knowing God as Father will change our understanding of prayer.

Understanding prayer as a means of fellowship with the father and a way of developing and maturing our relationship with him, will transform how and why we pray. Authentic fellowship with our father will cause the reorientation of our desires, hopes and dreams. We will be anxious to honour his name, we will want his kingdom to come, and we will desire to commit our lives to his will, because we understand that he is our father.

Knowing God as your Father will help you establish healthy priorities and motivations for living. Reading through Matthew 6 can be very daunting. Think of the kind of things Jesus asks of us in this chapter: -

We are to hallow Gods name

Pray that his kingdom will come

Ensure that his will be done

Forgive those who have hurt us

Live a life of dependence

Endeavour to avoid sin

Make sure that our treasure is in heaven not on earth

Avoid all worry,

Seek desperately for righteousness.

The important thing to understand is that guilt and condemnation cannot help or encourage us to do any of the above.

This kind of living is only possible as we discover that God really is our Father and He wants us to enjoy being his children.
prayer: Father may my relationship with you as my Father determine how I live and how I prioritise what is important.
